فثبت ممّا بيّنّا بالبرهان أنّ لا قوّةَ ولا استعدادَ بالذات لكون الشيء فاعلا ، بل إنّما القوّة والاستعداد للإنفعال ولصيرورة الشيء قابلا لشيء بعد أن لم يكن» ، إنتهى.

englishCorrections.new:
“From what we have demonstrated it is therefore established that there is intrinsically no capacity or preparedness for a thing's being an agent. Capacity and preparedness are only for being affected, and for a thing to become receptive to something after it had not been so.” End of quotation.

As for preparedness itself, it has been said: “It belongs to relation, since it is intelligible only between two things: something prepared and that for which it is prepared. It is therefore not a species of quality.” From some writers it appears that it is a quality entailing a relation, like knowledge, which belongs to the psychic qualities and entails a relation between its subject and its object—that is, the knower and the known—and like capacity and will.

old.text: At N-VI-16 the 1417 AH base reads «ينتزع من الموضوعين ... وصفاً ناعتاً لهما». The 1428 AH revised edition, vol. 1 p. 218 n. 4, explicitly corrects to «ينتزع لكلّ من الموضوعين ... وصفاً ناعتاً له», referring a separate relational predicate to each term rather than one quality belonging identically to both. Both panels follow the editor's reading, and the earlier wording is preserved here. The editor also notes that «لوقوعها» is preferable to «لوقوعه» in a preceding phrase; the main 1417 text already has «لوقوعها», so no correction was necessary there. In the same chapter, the editor also reports that the copies read «المضاف إلى الابن» but corrects to «المضاف إلى الأب» (vol. 1 p. 218 n. 1). In this passage a son is related to his father; ‘to a son’ contradicts the accompanying example of sonship. The online Arabic and English now adopt this explicitly recorded correction, retaining the older wording in the apparatus.
